tokens.TITLE: Shane Boyer x DJI: Gear Behind the POV
tokens.META_DESCRIPTION: Shane Boyer (@shaneboyerr) builds cinematic New York POV films with pro camera gear. Inside his craft, the DJI partnership DGTL lists, and how he gets the shot.
tokens.KEYWORDS: Shane Boyer, shaneboyerr, Shane Boyer DJI, DJI, camera gear, gimbal, POV filmmaker, cinematic New York, TikTok, content creator, influencer marketing
tokens.HEADLINE_GOLD: and the gear behind the POV.
tokens.DEK: The 11.7M-view films don't happen by accident. Shane Boyer's cinematic New York is built on real craft and pro camera tools — the reason DGTL pairs him with gear brands like DJI, and why the footage looks like a short film.
tokens.HERO_CAPTION: A frame from Shane Boyer's slow-motion New York work — the cinematic look built on pro gear. Courtesy @shaneboyerr / see more on TikTok.
tokens.STAT_FOOTNOTE: Follower/like/view figures verified July 2026 from Shane Boyer's own channels. DJI is listed among his brand partners per DGTL; the focus here is his verifiable craft and cinematic style.
tokens.LEAD: Shane Boyer (@shaneboyerr) makes New York look like a short film, and that doesn't happen on a phone held at arm's length. Behind the 11.7M-view Polaroid cut and the 2.5M+ following is real craft — stabilised moves, patient framing, careful colour — the kind of work that makes gear brands like DJI a natural fit, and the reason DGTL pairs him with camera partners.
tokens.BODY_1: Look closely at a Boyer video and the technique is doing quiet, deliberate work. The camera glides where a handheld shot would shake; the frame holds long enough to feel composed, not grabbed. That control is what separates a POV film from a POV clip — and it's the difference a pro toolset buys a creator who already has the eye.
tokens.H2_1: Craft is the reason the numbers exist
tokens.BODY_2: Boyer's signature moves — the ledge push-in, the platform pan as a train blurs by, the golden-hour glide over One World Trade — read as cinema because they're executed like cinema. Stabilisation, frame rate, and grade are the tools; taste is what points them. That combination is precisely what a gear brand wants associated with its name: not a spec demo, but proof of what the kit makes possible in the right hands.
tokens.PULLQUOTE: Anyone can point a camera at New York. Boyer builds the shot.
tokens.PULLQUOTE_CITE: — The DGTL Influence view on Shane Boyer
tokens.H2_2: Why gear brands fit a creator like this
tokens.BODY_3: Because the best hardware ad is a great piece of work made with it. A creator who already shoots at this level makes a camera or gimbal look capable without a single feature callout — the footage is the argument. That's the logic behind pairing Boyer with camera partners like DJI: put pro tools in the hands of someone whose output already sells the possibility. You can study the technique on his TikTok and Instagram.
tokens.CALLOUT_TITLE: Why gear brands fit Shane Boyer
tokens.CALLOUT_1: The footage is the ad — pro results without a single feature callout.
tokens.CALLOUT_2: Stabilised, cinematic moves that show what the kit makes possible.
tokens.CALLOUT_3: A creator with the eye already — gear amplifies, it doesn't carry.
tokens.CALLOUT_4: 2.5M+ followers who value craft, the right room for a camera brand.
tokens.BODY_4: For a gear brand, that's the whole appeal: the most persuasive proof of what a camera can do is a filmmaker who was going to make something beautiful anyway. Give Shane Boyer the tools and the receipts show up in the footage.
tokens.STATCALLOUT_CAP: 11.7M views on one film. Reach at that scale rides on craft — the stabilised, colour-graded, patiently framed look that pro gear enables in the right hands.

tokens.FAQ_Q1: What gear does Shane Boyer use?
tokens.FAQ_A1: Shane Boyer (@shaneboyerr) shoots stabilised, colour-graded cinematic footage rather than simple phone clips, using pro camera tools to achieve his signature POV look. DGTL lists DJI among his brand partners; his craft — framing, stabilisation and grade — is what defines the result.
tokens.FAQ_Q2: Why do camera brands work with creators like Shane Boyer?
tokens.FAQ_A2: Because a great piece of work is the most persuasive hardware ad. A creator who already shoots at a cinematic level makes a camera or gimbal look capable without feature callouts — the footage itself is the argument.
tokens.FAQ_Q3: How does Shane Boyer get his cinematic look?
tokens.FAQ_A3: Through craft: stabilised camera moves, patient framing that holds a shot until it feels composed, careful colour grading, and a filmmaker's eye for New York light. The gear amplifies technique he already has.
tokens.FAQ_A4: Shane Boyer is an American content creator and POV filmmaker known for cinematic New York City videos, with 2.5M+ TikTok followers and an 11.7M-view Polaroid brand film. His brand partners have included Polaroid, YSL, Canada Goose and Ray-Ban Meta.
